name: 401 KAR 5:065 Section 2(5): KPDES reporting of spills, bypasses, upsets
status_reason: The only overflow-reporting rule found: report to the Division of Water, no public notice duty.
notes: Quote: "Reporting shall be as established in 40 C.F.R. 122.41 except that: (a) If a spill or release of pollutants or contaminants, bypass, upset, or other event of noncompliance occurs that may present an imminent or substantial danger to the environment or the public health or welfare, the permittee shall immediately notify the Division of Water by calling the Division of Water in Frankfort at (502) 564-3410 or the appropriate regional field office ... (b) If a report required by this subsection is made during other than normal business hours, it shall be made through the twenty-four (24) hour environmental emergency telephone number". No duty to tell the public was found in the regulation.

name: EPA SOBE extract, Kentucky rows (state electronic reporting system, ES2)
operator: U.S. EPA ECHO (data from Kentucky DOW)
waters_covered: statewide in principle; 43 rows in practice
access_detail: Downloaded the ECHO ZIP (1.1 MB) on 2026-11-03; KY rows are electronic_submission_type ES2 'Authorized NPDES program electronic reporting system', form set ids KY-112xx; description text begins 'Incident ID: nnnnnnn' (the Cabinet's incident number). Trimmed sample (description omitted) raw/sobe-ky-sample-2026-11-03.json.
cadence: ECHO daily; but KY rows exist only for reports received 2025-12 (34) and 2026-01 (9); nothing since
status_reason: Proves Kentucky's state system can push events (with coordinates and incident ids) to EPA, but the flow stopped after January 2026. If it resumes this becomes Kentucky's statewide feed.
notes: Description text names individuals (reporters, responders); never ingest it unfiltered. Receiving water is mostly 'Unnamed Tributary or Unknown'. Structure type is always 'Other'. 43 rows, 37 permits including KY0022411 (Louisville MSD) and KY0021466 (SD1).

name: Louisville MSD Overflow Advisory Level banner and notice nodes
waters_covered: Ohio River and streams in Louisville Metro (Jefferson County)
access_detail: Advisory block on every page of louisvillemsd.org and at /overflowalert (raw/louisville-msd-overflowalert-2026-11-03.html). Each advisory is a Drupal node with a timestamp: node/31322 and node/31323 'MSD-01 Wet Weather Overflows.' stamped 'November 3, 2026 3:00 AM' (raw/louisville-msd-node-31322-2026-11-03.html). Search results show event nodes 'MSD-02 2/18/2025 A Wet Weather Discharge has occurred' with a start time, and 'MSD-02 4/6/2026 A Dry Weather Discharge has occurred.'; the 2025 node now returns 404, so old notices are removed.

sample_record.text: Recent rainfall has created the risk of sewer overflows in the Louisville Metro area. Avoid contact with water in the Ohio River, streams, drainage ditches and standing water until 48 hours after the rain has stopped.

cadence: set by MSD with rain; banner live on 2026-11-03
history: none kept on site (old nodes removed)
status_reason: Kentucky's most useful live notice: a dated system-wide advisory with a 48-hour after-rain rule, plus dated MSD-02 discharge notices. Needs a snapshot state machine (poll the banner, record level changes, follow node links).
notes: MSD also says 'For more information, go to www.msdprojectwin.org'. An email list signup is in the footer ('Water Quality Email List Signup'); not subscribed.

name: SD1 Wet Weather Overflow Notification Program (Northern Kentucky)
operator: Sanitation District No. 1 of Northern Kentucky
waters_covered: Ohio River, Licking River, Banklick Creek and other streams in Boone, Campbell and Kenton counties
access_detail: Page fetched (raw/sd1-wet-weather-notification-2026-11-03.html). Notifications by sign-up only (CivicPlus Notify Me); map of overflow areas PDF https://sd1.org/DocumentCenter/View/207/Local-Sewer-Overflows-PDF.
cadence: Quote: "We will only alert you during contact recreational season (May through October) when: Rainfall of 0.25 inches or more is recorded in SD1's service area, including Boone, Campbell and Kenton counties The Ohio River exceeds 38 feet"; "All advisories will remain in effect for 72 hours after rainfall or 72 hours after river levels drop below 38 feet."
status_reason: A rule-based advisory (rain or river stage), not an event report; the site can reproduce the rule itself from rain and river gauges. Owner sign-up needed to see the email format.
notes: SD1 posts CSO signs: "If you see these signs, avoid nearby water during and after rainfall for at least 72 hours." Its rule (0.25 inch, Ohio River 38 feet, 72 hours) matches the site's 72-hour yellow window.

name: Kentucky swimming advisories (DOW and Department for Public Health)
operator: Kentucky Division of Water / Cabinet for Health and Family Services
waters_covered: Upper Cumberland River, North Fork Kentucky River, Licking River (Banklick Creek, Three Mile Creek)
access_detail: Page fetched (raw/ky-dow-swimming-advisories-2026-11-03.html). Standing advisories 'in place for several years', no dates.
status_reason: Standing stream-reach advisories tied to sewage; show as authority advisories (red, quoted) on the named reaches.
notes: Quote: "People should avoid recreational contact with waters in the areas specified because of the bacteria, which occur in human and animal waste and indicate the presence of untreated or inadequately treated sewage." And: "The agencies also recommend against swimming or other full-body contact with surface waters immediately following heavy rainfall events ... due to an increased potential for exposure to ... bypasses from sewage collection systems, combined sewer overflows".
